description: Sofa.1 combines an intuitive dashboard for scheduled micro-check-ins with an empathetic voice chatbot. Powered by Edge AI, it processes data locally for fast, reliable monitoring. The chatbot collects vital information and analyzes speech for biomarkers of stress and fatigue. Using predictive analytics on multimodal data, Sofa.1 detects potential physical and mental health risks before symptoms appear, automatically triggering personalized action plans to support astronaut well-being and mission

Orchest

Space crew health sensor station — illustrated site guide

https://orbithealth-di4zhcqm.manus.space

Version 14 Nov 2026 · every screenshot was captured from the live site (camera + mic + keyboard actually running)

The Orchest home page before any tool is started

1. Overview

Orchest is a progressive web app that runs entirely in the browser, and everything lives in one sensor station: the camera watches the face, eyes, distance and zoom plus depression-related expressions, the microphone analyses the voice, and the keyboard analyses typing. All processing happens on the user's own device, measurements are kept in localStorage, and the app keeps working with no internet after the first visit.



Permanent site: https://orbithealth-di4zhcqm.manus.space



Fully English interface, LTR layout, product name Orchest.



No video or audio ever leaves the device: analysis is local.



An optional backend (.NET 10 + SignalR + SQL Server) handles sync; the app works fine without it.

2. Home page and summary

The header carries the logo, the name and a one-line description, with the connection pill (Online / Offline — still working) and the number of saved readings on the right. Below it sits the "Sensor Station — everything in one place" card with the last 24 hours, the latest mood score and the vision flag count, followed by the tool tabs: All tools, Vision & Gaze Camera, Mood & Depression Indicators, Voice Analysis and Typing Analysis.

The 24-hour summary: readings count, latest mood score and vision flags after measurements were saved

3. Camera and face tracking (Vision & Gaze)

Pressing Start camera opens the device camera; once the MediaPipe FaceLandmarker model loads, the app places 478 landmarks on the face and reads its blendshapes. The card shows the camera feed with the landmark mesh (core points in orange) and computes the following metrics many times per second:

Close-up of the camera feed: landmark mesh and face bounding box

4. Reading test and font zoom

The same card contains a reading passage whose font size is adjustable. If the user enlarges the text, zooms the browser or leans towards the screen, the inline flag "Font enlarged to 26px — a sign of reading difficulty" appears and the reading strain index rises (green below 35%, amber from 35%, red from 60%). This targets the SANS risk area (vision changes and reduced visual acuity) tracked by NASA HRP.

After enlarging the text to 26px: the inline flag appears, strain index reaches 40%, and the reading is saved

5. Depression indicators from facial expression

Below the camera sits an independent panel, "Depression indicators from face tracking", which aggregates facial expression over the camera session into a score from 0 to 100. Once the session passes 15 seconds the "Analyse mood & save result" button becomes active; the result is written to local history and forwarded to the backend when it is reachable.

The depression panel during a real camera session: live score 38/100 with every indicator value

Important: this score is a research signal derived from facial expression, not a medical diagnosis. If it stays high across sessions, the right next step is a PHQ-9 questionnaire and a clinician.

6. Voice analysis (Microphone & Voice)

The card asks the user to read a fixed sentence for 8 seconds. During recording a live waveform and countdown are shown; afterwards the app computes loudness (RMS in dB), pitch in Hz (autocorrelation), pitch jitter, pause ratio, the number of voice dropouts and the word error rate against the target sentence when SpeechRecognition is available.

Recording in progress: microphone live, waveform moving, countdown ticking

Result of a real spoken sentence: -18 dB, 153 Hz pitch, 22% pauses, 2 dropouts

7. Typing analysis (Keyboard & Accuracy)

The user types the displayed sentence character by character while the app tracks keystrokes, mistakes, backspaces and the intervals between keys. The result reports typing speed (wpm), error rate, correction rate, rhythm variation and accuracy. These numbers map to musculoskeletal (tremor) and motor/cognitive slowing risks.

8. Results, history and sync

"Latest results" lists the newest reading from each tool with its flags, next to the "How measurements map to indicators" card that links every measurement to a NASA HRP risk domain. Below them, "Measurement history on this device" keeps every reading with its timestamp and level, with a "Sync with server" button (active when the backend is reachable) and "Clear history".

Latest results beside the map from measurements to NASA HRP risk domains

Local measurement history: every reading with date, time and flags

9. Offline use and installation

After the first visit the service worker caches the app shell and the face model, so the page opens with no connection, the header switches to "Offline — still working" and previous readings stay visible. The camera also works offline once it has been opened online at least once.

After going offline and reloading: the app opens, shows "Offline — still working", and keeps its history

Installing on a phone: Android (Chrome) menu Install app / Add to Home screen. iPhone (Safari) →→ Share Add to Home Screen. Once installed it launches from the home screen like any native app.→

10. Mobile and tablet layout

Home screen at 390×844: header, summary card and tool tabs

Camera running on mobile: face detected and metrics shown under the video feed

11. How the project is built



Frontend: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7; PWA through vite-plugin-pwa (app-shell precache plus runtime caching for the model and wasm).



Analysis: MediaPipe FaceLandmarker (478 landmarks + blendshapes) in the browser; voice and typing metrics use Web Audio and plain JavaScript.



Scoring: src/sensors/evaluate.ts produces flags and a level (nominal / watch / urgent) with the same thresholds as the backend.



Storage: localStorage under the key orchest.sensors.v1, with optional sync to POST /api/sensors.



Backend: .NET 10 Minimal API + SignalR on /hub/health + EF Core 10 (SQL Server, InMemory fallback). Endpoints: /api/health, /api/state, /api/telemetry, /api/symptoms, /api/sensors, /api/reports, /api/demo/*.



Deployment: static build (npm ci && npm run build dist) on Manus hosting, with no →server or database.

12. Running locally (Windows)

The local package contains web/ (frontend), server/ (API) and two launchers. Requirements: Node.js 20/22 and the .NET 10 SDK, plus an optional SQL Server instance (without one the API falls back to InMemory).



start-server.bat API on http://localhost:5054 (check /api/health).→



start-web.bat frontend on http://localhost:5173; Vite proxies /api and /hub to 5054.→



Database: edit server\appsettings.json (ConnectionStrings:Default and Database:Provider).

Package: Orchest-Local.zip — verified here: 0 build errors, /api/health returned ok:true, and posting a mood reading returned 200.

13. Limits and notes



The depression score is a research signal from facial expression, not a diagnosis; it needs confirmation with PHQ-9 or a clinician.



The centimetre distance estimate is approximate (6.3 cm inter-ocular factor) and depends on the camera angle.



Speech clarity (WER) needs SpeechRecognition support (Chrome/Edge); otherwise it shows "—".



Running the camera and the microphone together slows the countdown on low-end devices, so stop the camera before recording voice.



All numbers in the screenshots come from automated test sessions: a test video for the camera, a synthetic spoken sentence for the microphone and scripted typing for the keyboard.

14. Built with Manus

Orchest was designed, built, tested and deployed end to end with Manus: the project plan and NASA HRP risk mapping, the React 19 + TypeScript frontend, the MediaPipe face-tracking and depression-indicator logic, the voice and typing analysis, the PWA/offline service worker, the .NET 10 + SignalR backend, the published site, and this illustrated guide with its screenshots were all produced in Manus sessions. Testing (camera, microphone, keyboard, offline reload) and the documentation captures were automated in the Manus sandbox.

Published site: https://orbithealth-di4zhcqm.manus.space

15. References

Risk domains, indicators and mapping are grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) material:



NASA HRP — Risks: https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/risks/



NASA HRP — Hazards: https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazards/



NASA HRP — Ongoing research: https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/ongoing-hrp-research/

Mapping in the app: visual strain and font zoom eyes & brain (SANS); frowning and little smiling →→mood and behaviour; weak or hoarse voice respiratory, mood and sleep; typing errors and tremor →→musculoskeletal and sensorimotor performance.
